definition: Pensive means engaged in deep, often somewhat wistful or melancholy thought.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pensive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pensive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: She grew pensive at the window as the last moving box was carried out.
Quiet is weaker than pensive: a quiet person may simply not be talking, while a pensive one is visibly absorbed in wistful thought.
Brooding is stronger than pensive — brooding suggests dark, heavy thoughts circled obsessively, while pensive thought stays gentle, tinged with melancholy rather than weighed down by it.

Thoughtful means absorbed in thought or careful in judgment, with no particular mood attached — a thoughtful pause can be perfectly cheerful. Pensive is thoughtful with a shadow: the thinking runs deep and carries a wistful, faintly sad tint. A thoughtful pause weighs options; a pensive one weighs memories.

Wistful names a feeling: quiet longing for something missed or out of reach, often with a soft smile. Pensive names a state of mind — deep, absorbed thought that carries that wistful shade without being only about longing. A wistful sigh misses something; a pensive silence is working through something.

On the morning of his last crossing, Captain Aldous ran the ferry exactly as he had for thirty-one years: lines cast off at seven, coffee at the wheel, the harbor swinging slowly into view.
But the deckhands noticed a change once the channel opened.
The jokes stopped, and the captain went pensive at the wheel, eyes on the water and somewhere else entirely.
He was turning over decades — the winter the engine failed mid-channel, the summer his daughter worked the ticket booth, a thousand identical mornings that no longer felt identical.
He answered every radio call crisply and made the dock on the minute.
It was the long, absorbed sorting of a man taking leave of something — a deep current of memory with a soft ache running through it.
